Three hundred denarii was therefore close to a year's wages, which explains the onlookers' indignation."},{"verse":9,"phrase":"good news","lemma":"εὐαγγέλιον","kind":"departure","traditional":"gospel","note":"The Greek was an ordinary word for a public announcement of good news, used also of imperial proclamations. Greek had a separate word for 'betray', which is not used here. It is intimate and direct without being childish."},{"verse":38,"phrase":"testing","lemma":"πειρασμός","kind":"departure","traditional":"temptation","note":"The Greek word covers both a trial that tests a person's faithfulness and an enticement to sin. In this scene the disciples face an ordeal that will prove their loyalty, so 'testing' is the nearer sense. Most translations have 'temptation'; some have 'the time of trial'."},{"verse":41,"phrase":"Enough!","lemma":"ἀπέχω","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"It is enough","note":"The single Greek word here is one of the most disputed in Mark. The preceding words can also be read as a command or an ironic concession ('Sleep on, then') and not as a question."},{"verse":47,"phrase":"slave","lemma":"δοῦλος","kind":"departure","traditional":"servant","note":"The word meant a person owned by another, and ancient hearers understood it so; 'servant' softens this. Several modern translations now use 'slave', while others keep 'servant' to avoid associations with modern race-based slavery. For the same reason the related word in verses 66 and 69, traditionally 'servant girl' or 'maid', is rendered 'slave girl'."},{"verse":48,"phrase":"bandit","lemma":"λῃστής","kind":"departure","traditional":"robber; thief","note":"The word denotes an armed brigand who uses violence, not a thief who works by stealth, and in this period it was also applied to insurgents. That explains the swords and clubs. The same word describes the two men crucified beside Jesus in the next chapter."},{"verse":58,"phrase":"sanctuary","lemma":"ναός","kind":"departure","traditional":"temple","note":"Greek has two words that English Bibles usually both render 'temple'. The one in verse 49 means the whole temple complex with its courts; the one here means the sanctuary building itself, the dwelling place of God. 'Sanctuary' keeps the two apart."},{"verse":61,"phrase":"the Messiah","lemma":"Χριστός","kind":"departure","traditional":"the Christ","note":"The high priest is asking whether Jesus claims a title: the anointed king Israel expected. 'Messiah' conveys that to a modern reader, whereas 'Christ' now sounds like a name. Several modern translations use 'Messiah' where the title is the point and 'Christ' elsewhere."},{"verse":62,"phrase":"the Power","lemma":"δύναμις","kind":"background","traditional":"Power; the Mighty One","note":"'The Power' is a reverent way of referring to God without naming him, as is 'the Blessed One' in the high priest's question. The reply combines two scriptures: the king seated at God's right hand in Psalm 110:1 and the figure 'like a son of man' who comes with the clouds of heaven in Daniel 7:13. It is this claim to share God's authority that the high priest calls blasphemy."},{"verse":68,"phrase":"and a rooster crowed","lemma":"","kind":"textual","traditional":"and the cock crew","note":"These words are missing from several important early manuscripts, and some editions bracket or omit them. The SBLGNT prints them without brackets, and they prepare for the 'second time' in verse 72. Scribes may have added them to supply a first crowing, or dropped them to match the other Gospels, which mention only one."},{"verse":70,"phrase":"and your speech is the same","lemma":"","kind":"textual","traditional":"and thy speech agreeth thereto","note":"This clause is absent from the earliest manuscripts and from many critical editions and modern translations. The SBLGNT includes it, so it is translated here."},{"verse":72,"phrase":"he broke down and wept","lemma":"ἐπιβάλλω","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"when he thought thereon, he wept; he broke down and wept","note":"The Greek participle literally means 'having thrown upon', and its sense here is uncertain. Proposals include 'when he reflected on it', 'he began to weep', 'he covered his head and wept', and 'he rushed out and wept'. 'Broke down' follows the majority of modern translations."}]}

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the Passover and the Festival of Unleavened Bread were two days away. The chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to seize him by stealth and kill him,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for they were saying,

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: “Not during the festival, or there may be an uproar among the people.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While he was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, reclining at table, a woman came with an alabaster jar of perfume, pure nard, very costly. She broke the jar and poured it over his head.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But some were saying indignantly to one another,

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: “Why this waste of the perfume?

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: This perfume could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they scolded her harshly.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Leave her alone. Why are you giving her trouble? She has done a good deed for me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want you can do good to them; but you do not always have me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: She did what she could: she has anointed my body ahead of time for its burial.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly I tell you, wherever the good news is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told, in memory of her.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went off to the chief priests to hand him over to them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they heard it they were glad, and they promised to give him money. So he began looking for a good opportunity to hand him over.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: On the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they sacrificed the Passover lamb, his disciples said to him,

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: “Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the Passover?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he sent two of his disciples and told them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Go into the city, and a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and wherever he goes in, say to the owner of the house, ‘The Teacher says: Where is my guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: He will show you a large upstairs room, furnished and ready. Prepare for us there.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The disciples set out and went into the city and found things just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When evening came, he arrived with the Twelve.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As they were reclining and eating, Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly I tell you, one of you will hand me over, one who is eating with me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They began to be grieved and to say to him, one after another,

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: “Surely not I?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “One of the Twelve, the one dipping with me into the bowl.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For the Son of Man goes just as it is written about him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would be better for that man if he had not been born.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While they were eating, he took bread, said a blessing, broke it, gave it to them and said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Take; this is my body.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he took a cup, gave thanks and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly I tell you, I will never again drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You will all fall away, for it is written: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But after I have been raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Peter said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Even if they all fall away, I will not.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly I tell you: today, this very night, before a rooster crows twice, you yourself will deny me three times.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he kept insisting all the more,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Even if I must die with you, I will never deny you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they all said the same.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They came to a place called Gethsemane, and he said to his disciples,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Sit here while I pray.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He took Peter, James and John with him, and he began to be filled with dread and deep distress.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “My soul is deeply grieved, to the point of death. Remain here and stay awake.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Going on a little farther, he fell to the ground and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Abba, Father, all things are possible for you. Take this cup away from me. Yet not what I want, but what you want.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He came and found them sleeping, and he said to Peter,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Simon, are you asleep? Did you not have the strength to stay awake one hour?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Stay awake and pray, so that you do not come into testing. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Again he went away and prayed, saying the same words.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And again he came and found them sleeping, for their eyes were very heavy, and they did not know what to answer him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He came the third time and said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Are you still sleeping and resting? Enough! The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Get up, let us go. Look, the one handing me over has come near.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, and with him a crowd with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests, the scribes and the elders.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the one handing him over had given them a signal, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “The one I kiss is the man. Seize him and lead him away under guard.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he came, he went up to him at once and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Rabbi!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and kissed him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They laid hands on him and seized him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But one of those standing by drew his sword, struck the high priest’s slave and cut off his ear.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them in response,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest me, as if against a bandit?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Day after day I was with you in the temple, teaching, and you did not seize me. But let the scriptures be fulfilled.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then they all left him and fled.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A certain young man was following him, wearing nothing but a linen cloth. They seized him,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but he left the linen cloth behind and fled naked.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests, the elders and the scribes assembled.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter had followed him at a distance, right into the high priest’s courtyard, and he was sitting with the attendants and warming himself at the fire.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The chief priests and the whole council were looking for testimony against Jesus in order to put him to death, and they were finding none.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For many were giving false testimony against him, but their testimonies did not agree.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then some stood up and gave false testimony against him, saying,

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: “We heard him say, ‘I will destroy this sanctuary made with hands, and in three days I will build another, not made with hands.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Yet not even so did their testimony agree.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the high priest stood up in their midst and questioned Jesus:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Have you no answer at all? What is it that these men are testifying against you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he stayed silent and gave no answer at all. Again the high priest questioned him and said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Are you the Messiah, the Son of the Blessed One?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am, and you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The high priest tore his clothes and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “What further need do we have of witnesses?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: You have heard the blasphemy. How does it look to you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they all condemned him as deserving death.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Some began to spit on him, to cover his face, to strike him with their fists and to say to him,

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: “Prophesy!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the attendants took charge of him with slaps.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the high priest’s slave girls came by.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Seeing Peter warming himself, she looked closely at him and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You too were with the Nazarene, Jesus.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he denied it, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I neither know nor understand what you are talking about.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He went outside into the forecourt, and a rooster crowed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The slave girl saw him and began again to say to those standing by,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This man is one of them.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But again he denied it. A little later those standing by again said to Peter,

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: “You really are one of them, for you are a Galilean, and your speech is the same.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he began to call down curses and to swear,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I do not know this man you are talking about.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At once a rooster crowed a second time. And Peter remembered the word Jesus had spoken to him:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Before a rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he broke down and wept.

notes.note: The adjective describing the nard is rare and its meaning is uncertain. Most scholars take it as 'genuine' or 'unadulterated', which is followed here. Other proposals are 'liquid' and a trade name for a particular variety of the plant.

notes.traditional: three hundred pence; a year's wages
notes.note: A denarius was a Roman silver coin, roughly a day's pay for a labourer. Three hundred denarii was therefore close to a year's wages, which explains the onlookers' indignation.

The Greek was an ordinary word for a public announcement of good news, used also of imperial proclamations. 'Gospel' now sounds like a religious term or a book title, so the plain meaning is given. Many modern translations alternate between the two.

The verb means to hand over or deliver up, and Mark uses the same word when the priests hand Jesus to Pilate and Pilate hands him over to be crucified. Greek had a separate word for 'betray', which is not used here. Most translations use 'betray' for Judas because the act was a betrayal; 'hand over' is kept throughout this chapter so the repeated verb stays visible.

Abba is the Aramaic word for 'father', which Mark preserves and then translates into Greek. It was used by adult children as well as small ones, so the popular claim that it means 'Daddy' is not supported by most scholars. It is intimate and direct without being childish.

The Greek word covers both a trial that tests a person's faithfulness and an enticement to sin. In this scene the disciples face an ordeal that will prove their loyalty, so 'testing' is the nearer sense. Most translations have 'temptation'; some have 'the time of trial'.

The single Greek word here is one of the most disputed in Mark. 'It is enough' is the usual rendering, but the verb is common in receipts meaning 'paid in full', so some read it as 'the account is settled' or as a reference to Judas having received his money. The preceding words can also be read as a command or an ironic concession ('Sleep on, then') and not as a question.

The word meant a person owned by another, and ancient hearers understood it so; 'servant' softens this. Several modern translations now use 'slave', while others keep 'servant' to avoid associations with modern race-based slavery. For the same reason the related word in verses 66 and 69, traditionally 'servant girl' or 'maid', is rendered 'slave girl'.

The word denotes an armed brigand who uses violence, not a thief who works by stealth, and in this period it was also applied to insurgents. That explains the swords and clubs. The same word describes the two men crucified beside Jesus in the next chapter.

Greek has two words that English Bibles usually both render 'temple'. The one in verse 49 means the whole temple complex with its courts; the one here means the sanctuary building itself, the dwelling place of God. 'Sanctuary' keeps the two apart.

The high priest is asking whether Jesus claims a title: the anointed king Israel expected. 'Messiah' conveys that to a modern reader, whereas 'Christ' now sounds like a name. Several modern translations use 'Messiah' where the title is the point and 'Christ' elsewhere.

'The Power' is a reverent way of referring to God without naming him, as is 'the Blessed One' in the high priest's question. The reply combines two scriptures: the king seated at God's right hand in Psalm 110:1 and the figure 'like a son of man' who comes with the clouds of heaven in Daniel 7:13. It is this claim to share God's authority that the high priest calls blasphemy.

These words are missing from several important early manuscripts, and some editions bracket or omit them. The SBLGNT prints them without brackets, and they prepare for the 'second time' in verse 72. Scribes may have added them to supply a first crowing, or dropped them to match the other Gospels, which mention only one.

notes.phrase: and your speech is the same
notes.note: This clause is absent from the earliest manuscripts and from many critical editions and modern translations. Many scholars think it was added under the influence of Matthew 26:73. The SBLGNT includes it, so it is translated here.

notes.traditional: when he thought thereon, he wept; he broke down and wept
notes.note: The Greek participle literally means 'having thrown upon', and its sense here is uncertain. Proposals include 'when he reflected on it', 'he began to weep', 'he covered his head and wept', and 'he rushed out and wept'. 'Broke down' follows the majority of modern translations.
